svg.title: YOLO26 clone architecture as implemented in baseline/yolo26clone
svg.desc: C3k2 backbone closing with SPPF and C2PSA, PAN-FPN neck, and an end-to-end anchor-free head with two parallel branches and no DFL. Shapes are for a 640x640 input and 2 classes. Module numbers follow the published YOLO26 layout.
svg.text: 9.949 M parameters at 2 classes (backbone 5.44 M · neck 3.57 M · Detect 0.93 M). Module numbers follow the published YOLO26 layout. Shapes are C×H×W for a 640×640 input, scale s (depth 0.50, width 0.50).

g.text: one per cell per level. No anchor boxes.
no DFL and no NMS. The panels
C3k2 — the CSP block, in place of YOLOv8's C2f
Same CSP shape as C2f; what changes is that each
branch may itself be a small C3, not a Bottleneck.
C2PSA — attention at the backbone end (10)
YOLOv8 has no counterpart: it ends at SPPF.
reg_max = 1 is the YOLOv8 difference that matters:
the box branch regresses the four distances directly,
so there is no 16-bin distribution and no DFL integral.
The one-to-many branch assigns up to 10 anchors per
object, which trains features well but leaves duplicates.
The one-to-one branch assigns 7 candidates and keeps
one, so its output needs no duplicate removal.
Inference reads one2one only. `postprocess` takes the
top 300 (anchor, class) pairs by score. That is all.
w decays 0.8 → 0.1 over training, so the shared trunk is
shaped early and the single-box branch dominates later.
Detect splits evenly between the two branches: 466,706 parameters each. The one-to-many half is training-only, so 4.7 % of the
network never runs at inference — and `Detector` skips it, which is worth about 1 ms per frame.
Every number here was read off the built model (`common/model.py`, scale s, 2 classes, 640 × 640 input), not from the published configuration.
Module indices are the reference's, so `state_dict` keys line up one-to-one with `ultralytics` — that is what `verify-clone` checks.
